Subject: Rackwise landing plan: node-grid sizing, rack wiring and storage carve-out

Hi Irene / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached is an updated rack layout and a preliminary node-grid capacity sheet based on our projected model mixes (70% generation, 30% embedding for the first 6 months). We're targeting two 42U racks for the initial pod and want Redwood's guidance on:

- node sizing (GPU mix and ephemeral vs. persistent storage split)
- suggested node-pool layout by tenant (our tenants are per-product line and require logical isolation)
- any recommended ignition scripts/host prep for NVMe passthrough and kernel tuning

Quick asks: can you validate the capacity assumptions in the NodeGrid tab (attached) and confirm whether Redwood prefers a single large PV class per rack or multiple SC classes per tenant?

Attachments: rackwise-rack-layout-v2.pdf (application/pdf), nodegrid-capacity-sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Tom Greer

Subject: Re: Rackwise landing plan: node-grid sizing, rack wiring and storage carve-out

Tom — thanks for the files and the clarity. Quick read-through notes below; we'll do a short sync to lock decisions.

Highlights / initial recommendations:
- Node sizing: for the mix you listed, we recommend a heterogenous fleet: 2x "generation-heavy" node types (A100 80GB + 1TB NVMe local for KV cache) and 1x "embed/aux" node type (A10/RTX 6000 class + smaller NVMe). This balances throughput and prefetch locality.
- Storage: avoid a single PV class per rack. Instead use two classes: fast local NVMe for KV/cache (ephemeral) and an encrypted blockstore class (network-attached) for long-term checkpoints. Tenants map to StorageClass by label (redwood.tenant=<tenant-name>).
- Node pools: suggest 3 pools initially — gen-heavy, embed-aux, infra (control/monitoring/egress). Use taints + nodeSelectors for pod placement; we'll share recommended taints.
- Network: L2 spanning within the rack, L3 across pods; egress NAT at the rack edge. We'll need the rack wiring diagram updated to show the external firewall IPs for static NAT.

Next steps: Marissa and I will draft a one-page "landing checklist" for your ops team that includes kernel knobs, bios settings, and the k8s StorageClass examples. Laura will help scope the preflight runbook. Could we do a 45-minute call on Wednesday 11/3 9:30am PT?

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Rackwise landing plan: node-grid sizing, rack wiring and storage carve-out

Tom — good question and glad you brought it up before fielding. Summary from the engineering side after our lab sim:

- Short answer: prefer single-rack affinity for the initial GA. Rationale: model KV cache locality and NVMe access patterns drive meaningful latency improvements when pods/processes are on the same rack and local NVMe is used. Cross-rack failsafe handled via checkpoint replication to the network blockstore.
- Production rollout plan: start with tenant scoped single-rack placement (fast path) and enable cross-rack anti-affinity for critical replicas only (replica placement policy in the rollout config).
- Failure mode: if an entire rack loses power, automatic failover to the other rack will rehydrate state from the encrypted blockstore; we recommend increasing checkpoint frequency to 10 minutes during rollout windows.

Action items (owned):
- Redwood (Irene/Marissa): provide the node taint/label recipes, kernel tuning script, and a sample StorageClass manifest by EOD Friday 11/12.
- Rackwise (Tom/Lisa): confirm PDU headroom and provide the firewall NAT pool IPs before 11/12.
- EdgeOps: confirm on-site provisioning timeline and whether they require the PXE images from us.

I'll attach the internal node-label cheatsheet after the call. If anything urgent changes on your side, ping me directly.

Thanks,
Irene
